intent.text:
I move that a draft plan like the vsect maturation plan be checked by one independent reviewer from another model family, and that the review be required to return concrete revisions, not a grade.

From the author and from later readers: a plan gets better only when someone who did not write it says what they would change — a missing step, a contradiction, an acceptance check the author would mark done without looking — and the author rewrites those sentences. The estate's own record is that independent checkers found defects in about 43% of landings that same-side rechecks had confirmed 116 of 116. Independence is what finds the holes; a different model family is the cheapest second set of blind spots.

A council's natural product is a decision. That grades the plan and leaves the sentences as they were. Later readers execute the document, not the minutes. One reviewer also gives the author a single coherent set of changes and a tight rewrite loop. Spread the same comments across seats and the author spends the round reconciling positions.

Hold a council only when that review surfaces a real choice the author cannot edit away — conflicting goals, or a constraint someone has to decide. Ordinary holes in a maturation plan are revisions, and they belong to one independent reader.
